intro: Bhutan climbs from subtropical foothills to Himalayan peaks over 7,000 m.

chapters.title: Valleys and peaks
text: Gangkhar Puensum, about 7,570 m, is the highest unclimbed mountain in the world, as climbing high peaks is banned. Most people live in deep river valleys.
Over 70% of the land is forest.

chapters.title: Carbon negative
text: Bhutan's forests absorb more carbon dioxide than the country produces, making it one of very few carbon-negative countries.

keyTerms.meaning: Removing more carbon dioxide than you produce.
